name: Practice Paper 4
subtitle: RRB Radiographer / X-Ray Technician — Advanced Mock (Level 8/10 · twisted language)

subsections.title: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which one of the following bones does NOT take part in forming the bony orbit?
questions.explanation: Seven bones form the orbit: frontal, sphenoid, zygomatic, maxilla, lacrimal, ethmoid and palatine. The nasal bone forms the bridge of the nose only.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The left kidney usually lies at a higher level than the right kidney.
2. The right main bronchus is shorter, wider and more vertical than the left.
3. The spleen lies in the right hypochondrium.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is true because the liver pushes the right kidney down. Statement 2 is true, which is why aspirated objects usually enter the right bronchus. Statement 3 is false: the spleen lies in the LEFT hypochondrium.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: A patient aspirates a peanut while sitting upright. On the chest radiograph, where is the foreign body MOST likely to have lodged?
options: Apical segment of the left upper lobe
Medial segment of the right middle lobe
Posterior basal segment of the right lower lobe
questions.explanation: The right bronchus is more vertical, and gravity carries the object to the most dependent segment when upright. In the supine position, the superior segment of the right lower lobe is more likely.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: All of the following pass through the foramen magnum EXCEPT:
options: Spinal roots of the accessory nerve
questions.explanation: The internal jugular vein leaves the skull through the jugular foramen, not the foramen magnum.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: A fracture through the surgical neck of the humerus seen on a shoulder radiograph puts which nerve at greatest risk?
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve winds around the surgical neck. The radial nerve is at risk in shaft fractures (spiral groove), and the ulnar nerve at the medial epicondyle.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: During a barium follow-through, the ligament of Treitz is used as a landmark for the:
questions.explanation: The suspensory ligament of the duodenum (Treitz) fixes the DJ flexure, normally to the left of L2. An abnormal position suggests malrotation.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A fracture through the waist of the scaphoid may lead to avascular necrosis of its proximal fragment.
Reason (R): The blood supply of the scaphoid enters mainly through its distal part and flows backwards towards the proximal pole.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. Because the vessels enter distally, a waist fracture cuts off the proximal pole, so R correctly explains A.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a content of the carpal tunnel?
questions.explanation: The ulnar nerve and artery pass through Guyon's canal, outside the flexor retinaculum.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The hepatic portal vein is formed behind the neck of the pancreas by the union of the:
options: Inferior mesenteric vein and superior mesenteric vein
Splenic vein and left gastric vein
Superior mesenteric vein and splenic vein
questions.explanation: The IMV usually drains into the splenic vein; the hepatic veins drain into the IVC, not the portal vein.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the sacrum is INCORRECT?
options: Its promontory projects into the pelvic inlet
It articulates with the ilia at the sacroiliac joints
It is formed by the fusion of four vertebrae
It has four pairs of anterior sacral foramina
questions.explanation: The sacrum is formed by five fused sacral vertebrae. The coccyx usually has four.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: On a frontal skull radiograph of an adult, a calcified pineal gland is useful mainly because:
options: It marks the position of the pituitary fossa
Its displacement from the midline suggests a space-occupying lesion
It indicates the level of the foramen magnum
questions.explanation: The pineal gland is a midline structure. If it shifts more than about 3 mm, it raises suspicion of a mass or haematoma.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: If a patient's cardiac output is 5 L/min at a heart rate of 70 beats/min, the stroke volume is approximately:
questions.explanation: Stroke volume = cardiac output ÷ heart rate = 5000 ÷ 70 ≈ 71 mL.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: An exposure of 80 kVp and 40 mAs at 100 cm FFD gives a satisfactory image. The FFD is increased to 150 cm and the kVp is raised to 92. Using the 15% rule, the new mAs needed is approximately:
questions.explanation: 92 kVp is about +15%, which halves the mAs to 20. The distance change multiplies it by (150/100)² = 2.25, so 20 × 2.25 = 45 mAs.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: Which change increases the NUMBER of photons produced at the target WITHOUT changing their maximum energy?
questions.explanation: mA changes only the quantity. kVp changes both quantity and maximum energy. Filtration removes photons, and FFD does not affect production.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: A tungsten-target tube is operated at 65 kVp. Which component will be ABSENT from the X-ray spectrum produced?
questions.explanation: Ejecting a K-shell electron in tungsten needs about 69.5 keV. At 65 kVp no electron has enough energy, so there are no K lines.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the anode heel effect:
1. It is more marked at a shorter FFD.
2. It is more marked with a larger image receptor.
3. It is more marked with a larger anode angle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Short FFD and a large field both include the steep part of the intensity gradient. A SMALLER anode angle (not a larger one) increases the heel effect, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: A beam has a half-value layer of 3 mm Al. What thickness of aluminium will reduce its intensity to 1/16 of the original?
questions.explanation: 1/16 = (1/2)⁴, which is 4 HVLs. 4 × 3 mm = 12 mm. (This assumes a monoenergetic beam; real beams harden.)

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The tenth-value layer (TVL) of a material is approximately equal to:
questions.explanation: TVL = ln10/μ and HVL = ln2/μ, so TVL/HVL = 2.303/0.693 ≈ 3.32.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: Which statement about Compton scattering is CORRECT?
options: Its probability rises steeply with Z³
Its probability is almost independent of atomic number and depends mainly on electron density
It needs photon energy above 1.02 MeV
The scattered photon has more energy than the incident photon
questions.explanation: Compton scattering involves loosely bound outer electrons, so tissue type matters less than electron density. This is why it reduces subject contrast.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: For the same exposure at the image receptor, which of the following would NOT reduce the patient's skin entrance dose?
options: Using a faster rare-earth screen or more sensitive detector
Raising the kVp and lowering the mAs
questions.explanation: A shorter focus-to-skin distance concentrates the beam on the skin (inverse square), so skin dose increases. The other three all reduce it.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The effective focal spot of a tube is 1 mm and the anode angle is 12° (sin 12° ≈ 0.21). The length of the actual focal spot is approximately:
questions.explanation: Effective = actual × sin θ, so actual = 1 / 0.21 ≈ 4.8 mm. This is the line focus principle.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: An object 4 cm wide lies 20 cm from the image receptor and the SID is 100 cm. What will be the width of its image?
questions.explanation: SOD = 80 cm, so M = SID/SOD = 100/80 = 1.25, and the image = 4 × 1.25 = 5 cm.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: With a 1.2 mm focal spot, a source-to-object distance of 90 cm and an object-to-image distance of 10 cm, the geometric unsharpness is about:
questions.explanation: Ug = focal spot × OID / SOD = 1.2 × 10 / 90 ≈ 0.13 mm.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Increasing kVp while reducing mAs generally lowers the patient dose for the same receptor exposure.
Reason (R): The probability of photoelectric absorption increases as kVp increases.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: A is true: more penetrating photons mean fewer are needed at the receptor. R is false: photoelectric absorption DECREASES with higher energy (∝ 1/E³), which is the real reason for the lower dose.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: At the same kVp setting, which generator produces the beam with the HIGHEST average photon energy?
questions.explanation: Less ripple means the voltage stays near its peak for longer, which gives a harder beam and more output per mAs.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: On a tube rating chart, which factor allows a HIGHER maximum mA for the same exposure time and kVp?
options: Using a lower anode rotation speed
questions.explanation: A larger focal track area spreads the heat. Lower rotation speed and higher kVp both REDUCE the permitted mA.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: Off-focus (extrafocal) radiation reaching the image is best reduced by:
options: First-stage collimator shutters placed as close as possible to the tube port
questions.explanation: Off-focus X-rays come from parts of the anode outside the focal spot. Shutters close to the source block them; a grid mainly removes patient scatter.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: An absorbed dose of 1 Gy from alpha particles (radiation weighting factor = 20) corresponds to an equivalent dose of:
questions.explanation: Equivalent dose (Sv) = absorbed dose (Gy) × wR = 1 × 20 = 20 Sv. X-rays and gamma rays have wR = 1.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: A patient with suspected acute sinusitis is to be checked for an air–fluid level in the maxillary antra. Which condition is ESSENTIAL for the occipitomental (Waters) view?
options: Patient supine with a 30° caudal angle
Patient prone with a 15° cephalic angle
Patient supine with a vertical beam
Patient erect with a horizontal central ray
questions.explanation: A fluid level is shown only when the beam is parallel to the fluid surface. If the patient cannot sit up, a horizontal-beam lateral can be used instead.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a criterion of a correctly positioned and exposed PA chest radiograph?
options: Scapulae projected over the lung fields
Medial ends of the clavicles equidistant from the spinous processes
About ten posterior ribs visible above the diaphragm
Thoracic vertebrae faintly visible through the heart shadow
questions.explanation: In a good PA chest the scapulae are rotated OFF the lung fields. The other three show no rotation, full inspiration and correct exposure.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: The Haas method (PA axial, 25° cephalad) is used as an alternative to which projection?
questions.explanation: Haas shows the occipital bone and dorsum sellae like Towne's, and it lowers the dose to the eyes and thyroid.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: A trauma patient is on a spine board with a cervical collar. On the horizontal-beam lateral, the shoulders hide C7. What should the radiographer do FIRST (if there is no contraindication)?
options: Remove the collar and flex the neck
Turn the patient prone for a vertical-beam lateral
Apply gentle downward traction on both arms and repeat the horizontal-beam lateral
Abandon the lateral and take only an AP open-mouth view
questions.explanation: Pulling the shoulders down usually shows C7–T1. If it fails, a horizontal-beam Swimmer's view or CT follows. The neck must never be moved.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: In which of the following projections is the central ray angled CAUDALLY?
questions.explanation: Towne's uses 30° caudad. The clavicle (15–30°), calcaneum (40°) and sacrum (15°) projections are all angled cephalad.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: On an AP forearm radiograph, the radius is seen crossing over the ulna. The MOST likely positioning error is that the:
questions.explanation: In pronation the radius crosses the ulna. An AP forearm needs full supination so that the two bones lie parallel.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: On a lateral knee radiograph, the femoral condyles are not superimposed because the medial condyle is projected below the lateral. The usual correction is to:
questions.explanation: The medial condyle extends lower than the lateral, so a slight cephalic angle superimposes them.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: Which projection is CONTRAINDICATED in an acute trauma patient until a cervical fracture or instability has been excluded?
questions.explanation: Flexion–extension views move the spine on purpose and could displace an unstable injury. They are done only after a radiologist or clinician has cleared the spine.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: On an AP pelvis, the lesser trochanters are clearly seen in profile and the femoral necks look short. This means that:
options: The limbs were correctly internally rotated 15°–20°
The central ray was angled cephalad
The lower limbs were externally rotated (not internally rotated)
The patient was rotated towards the left
questions.explanation: With 15°–20° internal rotation, the lesser trochanters are hidden or barely seen and the femoral necks are shown in full length.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: On a PA skull projection, the petrous ridges completely fill the orbits. The central ray must have been:
questions.explanation: At 0° the petrous ridges fill the orbits. With 15° caudad (Caldwell) they move to the lower third of the orbits.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: To demonstrate the RIGHT intervertebral foramina of the cervical spine using a posterior oblique projection, the patient should be placed in:
questions.explanation: Posterior obliques show the foramina FARTHEST from the IR, so the right side is up in LPO, with a cephalic angle. Anterior obliques show the side closest to the IR and use a caudal angle.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. In anterior oblique projections of the cervical spine, the intervertebral foramina CLOSEST to the IR are shown.
2. In posterior oblique projections of the lumbar spine, the zygapophyseal joints CLOSEST to the IR are shown.
3. In anterior oblique projections of the lumbar spine, the zygapophyseal joints FARTHEST from the IR are shown.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct. This is a classic trap: the cervical and lumbar oblique rules are the reverse of each other.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: An erect abdomen radiograph taken to look for free intraperitoneal air MUST include the:
questions.explanation: Free gas collects under the diaphragm, so the diaphragm domes must be on the image. A KUB, by contrast, must include the symphysis pubis.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: The Von Rosen projection (hips abducted 45° with internal rotation) is used to assess:
options: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis in trauma
questions.explanation: It helps assess the hip joint in infants and young children with suspected DDH. Ultrasound is preferred in early infancy.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: After a punch to the eye, an orbital floor 'blow-out' fracture with a 'hanging-drop' sign is BEST shown on the:
questions.explanation: Waters shows the orbital floors and maxillary antra, where herniated orbital contents look like a teardrop. CT confirms the fracture.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: For an AP projection of the coccyx, the central ray is directed:
options: 10° caudad, about 5 cm above the symphysis pubis
15° cephalad, midway between the ASIS and the symphysis
questions.explanation: The coccyx curves forward, so it needs a caudal angle. The sacrum uses about 15° cephalad.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: A processed film shows a general increase in density (chemical fog). All of the following are possible causes EXCEPT:
options: Unsafe safelight or a light leak in the darkroom
questions.explanation: Exhausted developer gives LIGHTER, under-developed films. Heat, overdevelopment and light leaks all increase fog.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: Months after processing, some radiographs develop yellowish-brown stains. The MOST likely cause is:
questions.explanation: Retained hypo breaks down to silver sulphide over time, which shows as brown staining that spoils archived films.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: The 'speed' of a radiographic film is conventionally defined as the reciprocal of the exposure needed to produce a density of:
questions.explanation: Speed = 1 / exposure at D = 1.0 + base + fog. Faster films sit to the LEFT on the H&D curve.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A wide-latitude film is often preferred for chest radiography.
Reason (R): Wide-latitude films have very high contrast.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: A is true: wide latitude records both dense mediastinum and lucent lungs. R is false: latitude and contrast are inversely related, so wide latitude means LOW contrast (a shallow gamma).

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: In computed radiography, a faint residual image from the previous patient appears on a new image. This 'ghost' artefact is due to:
options: Incomplete erasure of the imaging plate
questions.explanation: The erasure light must fully clear the stored energy. A stationary grid aligned with the laser scan causes moiré, not ghosting.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: For the same field of view, increasing the image matrix from 512 × 512 to 1024 × 1024 will:
options: Increase pixel size and reduce noise only
Reduce pixel size and improve spatial resolution, but increase file size
questions.explanation: Pixel size = FOV / matrix. Smaller pixels resolve finer detail but need four times the data.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: The parameter that describes how efficiently a digital detector converts incident X-ray quanta into useful image signal is the:
questions.explanation: A higher DQE means less dose is needed for the same image quality. MTF describes resolution.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: On a Fuji-type CR system, a HIGHER 'S' (sensitivity) number displayed after processing indicates:
options: HIGHER exposure to the imaging plate
LOWER exposure to the imaging plate
questions.explanation: The Fuji S-number is inversely proportional to exposure. A high S suggests underexposure (noise); a low S suggests overexposure. Some other vendors' exposure indices work the opposite way.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stochastic effects have a threshold dose below which they do not occur.
2. The severity of deterministic effects increases with dose.
3. Hereditary (genetic) effects of radiation are stochastic.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Stochastic effects (cancer, hereditary) are assumed to have NO threshold, and only their probability rises with dose. Deterministic effects have a threshold, and their severity rises with dose.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: A radiographer standing 1 m from the patient receives 4 µSv during a fluoroscopy procedure. In a repeat procedure she stands 2 m away and the screening time is halved. Her dose will now be about:
questions.explanation: Doubling the distance gives ¼ of the dose (inverse square), and halving the time gives ½ more. 4 × ¼ × ½ = 0.5 µSv.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: According to the law of Bergonié and Tribondeau, which of the following is the LEAST radiosensitive?
questions.explanation: Highly differentiated, non-dividing cells such as neurons and muscle are the most radioresistant.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT, by itself, considered a contraindication to iodinated contrast media?
options: A previous moderate-to-severe reaction to iodinated contrast
questions.explanation: There is no specific cross-reaction between seafood allergy and iodinated contrast. Any allergic history only slightly raises general risk. The other three need real precautions.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: According to ESUR guidelines, a 'late' (delayed) adverse reaction to iodinated contrast is one occurring:
options: Between 1 hour and 1 week after injection
questions.explanation: Acute reactions occur within 1 hour, late reactions between 1 hour and 1 week (often skin rashes), and very late reactions after 1 week (e.g., NSF with gadolinium, thyrotoxicosis).

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: During a barium swallow, the patient coughs violently and the screen shows barium outlining the bronchial tree. The MOST appropriate immediate action is to:
options: Give more barium to clear the oesophagus quickly
Lay the patient flat supine to drain the lungs
Inject IV contrast to assess the bronchi
Stop the examination, sit the patient upright, encourage coughing and inform the radiologist
questions.explanation: Aspiration needs the procedure stopped, the airway cleared (coughing or physiotherapy) and clinical review. Water-soluble high-osmolar agents are especially dangerous if aspirated.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: A T-tube cholangiogram is performed mainly to:
options: Assess gall bladder function before cholecystectomy
Check for retained common bile duct stones and free drainage into the duodenum before the T-tube is removed
Show the pancreatic duct during ERCP
questions.explanation: Contrast is injected through the T-tube left after CBD exploration, usually about 7–10 days after surgery.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: Hysterosalpingography is contraindicated in all of the following situations EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Infertility is the main INDICATION for HSG. Infection, pregnancy and active bleeding are contraindications.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: In digital subtraction angiography (DSA), the 'mask' image is:
options: The image with maximum contrast opacification
A lead mask placed over the patient's eyes
An image acquired before contrast arrives, which is subtracted from the later contrast images
The image after the contrast has washed out
questions.explanation: Subtraction removes bone and soft tissue, leaving only the opacified vessels. Patient movement causes misregistration artefacts.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: During C-arm fluoroscopy in a lateral projection, which practice will INCREASE the operator's dose?
options: Using last-image-hold instead of repeated screening
Standing on the X-ray tube side of the patient
Using pulsed rather than continuous fluoroscopy
Keeping the image intensifier close to the patient
questions.explanation: Scatter is highest where the beam enters the patient, on the tube side. Staff should stand on the image intensifier (detector) side.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: On a non-contrast CT, a well-defined lesion measures −80 HU. It is MOST likely composed of:
questions.explanation: Fat measures about −50 to −100 HU (e.g., lipoma). Simple fluid is 0 to +20, fresh blood +50 to +80 and calcification above +100 HU.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: In helical CT, increasing the pitch from 1.0 to 1.5 while keeping the mAs per rotation constant will:
options: Shorten scan time and reduce patient dose, with some loss of z-axis resolution
Have no effect on scan time
questions.explanation: The table moves 1.5 times the beam width per rotation, so less of the patient is overlapped and irradiated.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: Which MRI sequence nulls the signal from CSF and is especially useful for showing periventricular white-matter lesions?
questions.explanation: FLAIR suppresses fluid signal (bright T2 lesions next to dark CSF). STIR suppresses fat.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: On a T2-weighted spin-echo MR image, which of the following appears BRIGHT?
questions.explanation: Water and CSF are bright on T2. Cortical bone and air give almost no signal, and fast-flowing blood shows a dark flow void.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: Which of the following items can be SAFELY taken into MRI Zone IV?
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic objects become dangerous projectiles in the magnet room. Only MR-Safe (or MR-Conditional, under stated conditions) items may enter.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: Which ultrasound artefact helps to confirm that an echogenic focus in the gall bladder is a gallstone?
questions.explanation: A stone strongly reflects or absorbs sound, leaving a dark shadow behind it. Posterior enhancement is typical of a fluid-filled cyst.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: Changing an ultrasound transducer from 3.5 MHz to 7.5 MHz will:
options: Have no effect on image quality
Improve axial resolution but reduce depth of penetration
questions.explanation: Higher frequency means shorter wavelength (better resolution) but more attenuation (less penetration).

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: In a nuclear medicine generator ('cow'), Tc-99m is obtained from the decay of:
questions.explanation: Mo-99 (half-life about 66 h) decays to Tc-99m, which is eluted with saline.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which one of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
questions.explanation: The Rail Wheel Factory is at Yelahanka (Bengaluru). Kapurthala has the Rail Coach Factory.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution.
2. One-third of its members retire every second year.
3. The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct (Articles 83(1) and 89).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right under the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed property from Part III. It is now only a constitutional/legal right under Article 300A.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Non-Cooperation Movement
2. Dandi March
3. Quit India Movement
4. Partition of Bengal
questions.explanation: Partition of Bengal (1905), Non-Cooperation (1920), Dandi March (1930), Quit India (1942).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which of the following rivers does NOT flow westward into the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: The Mahanadi flows east into the Bay of Bengal. Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which Indian state shares its boundary with the largest number of other states?
questions.explanation: UP borders 8 states (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar) plus the NCT of Delhi.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Who among the following was NOT a member of the Cabinet Mission of 1946?
questions.explanation: Mountbatten came in 1947 as the last Viceroy. The Cabinet Mission had Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps and Alexander.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The 'Fairy Queen', which holds a Guinness World Record, is:
options: The longest goods train run in India
The oldest working steam locomotive in the world
questions.explanation: Built in 1855, the Fairy Queen is preserved by Indian Railways and still runs occasionally.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which one of the following trophy–sport pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
questions.explanation: Davis Cup is tennis, Ryder Cup is golf and Santosh Trophy is football.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India submits the audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union to the:
options: President, who causes them to be laid before Parliament
Speaker of the Lok Sabha directly
questions.explanation: Under Article 151, Union reports go to the President and State reports to the Governor.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A train 180 m long running at 54 km/h crosses a platform in 20 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation: 54 km/h = 15 m/s, and the distance covered = 15 × 20 = 300 m. Platform = 300 − 180 = 120 m.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: The price of petrol rises by 25%. By what percentage must a family reduce its consumption to keep its expenditure unchanged?

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become four times itself?
questions.explanation: Doubling means 100% interest in 5 years, so the rate is 20% p.a. Four times means 300% interest, which takes 15 years.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A and B together can do a work in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. In how many days can A alone do it?

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: The average of 11 results is 50. The average of the first six is 49 and that of the last six is 52. What is the sixth result?
questions.explanation: (6 × 49) + (6 × 52) − (11 × 50) = 294 + 312 − 550 = 56. The sixth result is counted in both groups.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: By selling an article for ₹720, a shopkeeper loses 10%. At what price should he sell it to gain 15%?

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 4, 6, 12, 30, 90, ?
questions.explanation: The multipliers are ×1.5, ×2, ×2.5, ×3, so next is ×3.5: 90 × 3.5 = 315.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: In a certain code, RADIATION is written as NOITAIDAR. How is SHIELDING written in that code?
questions.explanation: The word is written in reverse: S-H-I-E-L-D-I-N-G becomes G-N-I-D-L-E-I-H-S.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: If 'P + Q' means P is the father of Q, 'P − Q' means P is the wife of Q, and 'P × Q' means P is the brother of Q, which expression shows that M is the mother of N?
questions.explanation: M − K means M is K's wife; K + N means K is N's father. So M is N's mother.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing North. C is in the middle. A is to the immediate left of C. E is at the extreme right end. B is to the left of A. Who is sitting between C and E?
questions.explanation: From left to right: B, A, C, D, E. So D sits between C and E.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: If the velocity of a moving body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv², so KE ∝ v² and (2)² = 4.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Work (F·s) is a scalar dot product. The others have both magnitude and direction.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Among the following, which electromagnetic radiation has the LONGEST wavelength?
questions.explanation: In order of increasing wavelength: γ < X-ray < UV < visible < IR < microwave < radio.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which statement about the isotopes of hydrogen is CORRECT?
options: Tritium has one proton and two neutrons
questions.explanation: Protium has 1p and 0n, deuterium 1p and 1n, and tritium 1p and 2n. Tritium is radioactive (β⁻, half-life about 12.3 years).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following non-metals is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: In graphite each carbon uses three electrons for bonding, leaving one free (delocalised) electron to carry current.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which one of the following diseases is NOT caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: TB is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which hormone is known as the 'emergency' or 'fight-or-flight' hormone?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline from the adrenal medulla raises heart rate, blood glucose and blood flow to muscles.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A solution of pH 3, compared with a solution of pH 5, has a hydrogen-ion concentration that is:
questions.explanation: pH is logarithmic: a difference of 2 units means 10² = 100 times the [H⁺].

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Two thin lenses of power +2 D and −0.5 D are placed in contact. The focal length of the combination is about:
questions.explanation: P = 2 − 0.5 = +1.5 D, so f = 1/1.5 m ≈ 66.7 cm. A positive power means converging.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer is mainly caused by:
questions.explanation: UV light releases chlorine radicals from CFCs, and these destroy ozone catalytically. The Montreal Protocol (1987) phases them out.
